solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Manage command post

definitions.meaning: to manage something is to have charge of it and direct it
the centre from which an operation is directed

explanation.surface: An order to take charge of a military headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a verb for directing affairs and a noun for the headquarters that directs them.

clue.text: Child having unusual dread of cheese

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of dread in an odd order

explanation.surface: A child who has an odd fear of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' is the anagram signal for dread; CH is a standard abbreviation for child.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese, so it is an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Girl shown up as seductress

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the words that follow are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
a siren is a seductress

explanation.surface: A girl is exposed as a temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' turns AS SIREN backwards in this down entry. Nerissa is Portia's maid in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Mount carrying good saddle

indicators.note: carrying means the ride holds the letter for good

parts.note: to mount a horse is to ride

explanation.surface: A horse bearing a decent saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads saddle as horse tack; here it is a dip between two peaks along a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a low point along a ridge between summits, so the words are near synonyms in geography.

clue.text: French cow by rear of estate car

parts.note: the Limousin is a French breed of cattle

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of estate

explanation.surface: A French cow standing behind an estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate car' looks like one phrase (British for a station wagon), but car alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, so it is an example of a car.

clue.text: Baseball player in jug

definitions.meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter
a large vessel with a handle and lip for pouring

explanation.surface: A ballplayer somehow found inside a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the thrower on a baseball diamond and a pouring vessel, a double sense.

clue.text: Chaplain in flat on outskirts of Rome

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

indicators.note: outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Rome

explanation.surface: A chaplain living in an apartment on the edge of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is an informal name for a military chaplain, a synonym.

clue.text: Transmission of data from me in letter confused Yard?

indicators.note: confused shows the letters of me and letter are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard is muddled by a letter sent from me about data links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ME and LETTER into TELEMETR; Y for Yard ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemetry is the automatic recording and sending of measurements from a distance, so a kind of data transmission.

clue.text: Woman's legal action, we hear, is hairy

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: a woman's lawsuit is her suit

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a woman's lawsuit is a shaggy affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute is a formal word meaning covered in hair, a synonym of hairy.

clue.text: Consideration shown by some Yorkshire spectators

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fans in Yorkshire display regard for the players.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in YorkshiRE and continues through SPECTators.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is regard or esteem displayed towards someone, so it is consideration shown.

clue.text: What Macmillan eventually had, nasty ordeal ending in defeatism

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word ordeal has been roughed up into a new order
ending in points to the final letter of defeatism

explanation.surface: A remark on a prime minister's late reward after a grim ordeal finished in defeatism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns ORDEAL into EARLDO; 'ending in' adds M, the last letter of defeatism. Harold Macmillan, British prime minister, became Earl of Stockton late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Macmillan was created Earl of Stockton in 1984, so the title-holder's rank and lands are what he finally held.

clue.text: Spanish girl to perform a variety of roles

parts.note: to perform is to do

indicators.note: a variety of signals that the letters of roles appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A Spanish actress is asked to take on several different parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' is the anagram signal; 'to' is just a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Spanish female given name, so it is an example of a Spanish girl's name.

clue.text: Shame sappers during argument

indicators.note: during means the sappers come in the middle of the argument

parts.note: an argument is a dispute
RE is the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers

explanation.surface: Military engineers squabbling bring dishonour on the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in the British Army they are the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall into disrepute is to be in disgrace, so the word is a synonym for shame.

clue.text: Creature in middle of foaming river at York

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of foaming

parts.note: the Ouse is the river that flows through York

explanation.surface: Some creature is spotted in the frothing waters of a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the seven-letter foaming is M. York is a city in northern England on the River Ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent is a kind of creature, so the definition is a general term for the answer.

clue.text: Genuine male domain

parts.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: A man's territory that is truly his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or sphere of activity is a domain, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Turmoil caused by wizard holding Latin mass

indicators.note: holding means the wizard contains the Latin letter

parts.note: a maestro is a wizard or master of an art

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when a sorcerer conducts a Latin service.
explanation.walkthrough: Wizard looks like a magician but is a virtuoso, MAESTRO; mass is the physics symbol M, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool and figuratively a state of turmoil.

clue.text: I'm one being treated in hospital in a hurry

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a patient is someone receiving hospital treatment

explanation.surface: A hospital patient complains that they want to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a pun: the patient on the ward is anything but patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and eager for things to happen is in a hurry, an adjectival phrase matching the adjective.

clue.text: Book penned by drudge after revolutionary op, book having little literary quality

indicators.note: after means the drudge part comes after the turned op
revolutionary means the word op is turned round

parts.note: taken as written, short for operation

indicators.note: penned by means the book letter is enclosed by the drudge

parts.note: a drudge is a toiler

explanation.surface: A hack writer churns out a book after a revolutionary operation, of poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns op round; 'penned by' encloses the book letter in the drudge, after the first T, giving TBOILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a work written quickly for money, so it is a book of little literary merit.

clue.text: Account of soldiers in country close to defeat

parts.note: a country is a state
soldiers are men

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of defeat

explanation.surface: A report on troops stationed in a nation on the brink of defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' supplies T, the final letter of defeat; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a written or spoken account of events, as given to police or a bank.

clue.text: National theme

definitions.meaning: a citizen of a country, as in a British national

explanation.surface: A country's topic for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a citizen under a monarch's rule and the matter being discussed.

clue.text: Caviare possibly causes greed

indicators.note: possibly suggests caviare could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Fancy fish eggs may make people grasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a synonym of greed.

clue.text: Poet certainly needs a little time inside

indicators.note: inside means a and T go within the word for certainly

parts.note: certainly as a reply means yes
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A poet surely requires a short while to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet; 'a little time' is A plus T, placed inside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: William Butler Yeats was a celebrated Irish poet, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Disturb soldier in a gallery

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside a Tate

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier causes a disturbance in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries; GI, a US soldier, sits after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or trouble, a verb synonym of disturb.

clue.text: 24-carat American gold coin

parts.note: 24-carat gold is pure or solid gold

explanation.surface: A pure American gold piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The solidus was a gold coin of the late Roman and Byzantine empires, so it is a kind of gold coin.

clue.text: Runs into singer making money

indicators.note: into says runs goes inside the singer

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest voice
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Encountering a vocalist proves lucrative.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is British slang for money; 'Runs into' reads as meeting by chance but puts R inside BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang this word means cash, so it is an informal synonym for money.

clue.text: Bird annoyed by account

parts.note: annoyed means cross
a bill is an account to be paid

explanation.surface: A bird is irritated by an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch whose bill tips cross over, so this is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Beast of burden arrived, then left

parts.note: arrived means came

explanation.surface: A pack animal turned up and then departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel carries loads across deserts, so it is an example of a beast of burden.

clue.text: Church council contributing to controversy, no doubt

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A church assembly is surely adding to a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in controverSY and continues through NO Doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy, so it is a church council by definition.

clue.text: English farm animals bring about witty remark

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
a ram is a farm animal too

explanation.surface: English livestock somehow provoke a clever quip.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short pointed saying, so it is a synonym for a witty remark.

clue.text: There's grease around any ship's rope

indicators.note: around means the grease goes on both sides of any

parts.note: lard is animal fat, a grease

explanation.surface: Any rope on a ship is coated in grease.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cord or rope used on board ship to secure things, so it names a ship's rope.

clue.text: Hot in leather, male

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run leather, male

explanation.surface: A man feels warm dressed in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of leather into male.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, so it stands as an adjective for hot.

clue.text: Put right about costume

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a dress is a costume

explanation.surface: A wardrobe mistress fixes something about a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to correct it, a verb synonym of put right.
